name: Silberbergwerk Schwaz
kurzbeschreibung: The 'Mother of all Mines' in Schwaz takes visitors aboard a mine train deep into the medieval silver mountain of Europe's wealthiest mining town.
beschreibung:
Overview

The historic Schwaz Silver Mine in the lower Inn Valley is famously revered as the "Mother of all Mines" and ranks among Central Europe's most significant industrial monuments. During the late Middle Ages and the Renaissance, particularly throughout the 15th and 16th centuries, Schwaz was the preeminent global hub of silver and copper extraction. Up to 85 percent of all silver traded globally originated from the deep galleries carved into the Schwazer Falkenstein mountain. These immense riches made Tyrol one of Europe's wealthiest lands, bankrolling the Habsburg empire and the Fugger merchant dynasty. Today, the show mine provides an immersive journey into the gritty subterranean world of medieval miners.

Route & Requirements

The underground adventure begins with an exhilarating ride aboard the authentic electric pit railway, carrying passengers 800 meters deep into the Sigmund-Ernst gallery. From there, an informative 90-minute guided walking tour winds through narrow passages hand-chiseled into solid dolomite rock, cavernous extraction chambers, and past immense historical water wheels. Underground, a constant temperature of 12 degrees Celsius prevails year-round with high humidity. Warm clothing (jacket and long pants) and sturdy flat walking shoes are strictly required. Safety helmets and protective capes are provided upon entry. The tour is well-suited for children aged 4 and older, though due to underground rock terrain, it is not wheelchair accessible.

Visit & Arrival

The silver mine is open daily year-round (summer roughly 09:00 to 17:00, winter 10:00 to 16:00; guided departures on schedule). Admission is approximately €19.00 for adults and €11.00 for children. Reaching the mine by car: follow the Inntal autobahn A12 to the Schwaz exit, then follow the signposts toward Silberbergwerk. Free visitor parking is located directly at the mine terminal. Arriving by train: take ÖBB trains to Schwaz station; local city buses connect directly to the Silberbergwerk stop, or visitors can enjoy a pleasant 20-minute walk through town.

Tips

Given the immense popularity during school holiday periods, advance online ticket reservation with a designated tour time slot is strongly advised. Following your underground exploration, stroll through the picturesque medieval center of Schwaz with its gothic townhouses and Fugger palaces, and unwind in a traditional Tyrolean inn.
preis: Adults approx. €19.00, children (4-14) approx. €11.00, family tickets available
